items.title: Thomas Andrew Dorsey Interview, 1980-08-06
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Did you know a New Orleans gospel singer, Bessie Griffin? Bessie Griffin? Yeah, I knew.

ctx.x: Well I came here with the National Baptist Convention, that's one of the biggest organizations in the country. Come here with him, played for him. Remember that? Remember that? He helped him to bring the musicians out, I mean, teach the musicians. And we'd start on that, and of course it didn't be very much for us. We'd start on that three or four weeks before convention time. Getting these folk together, they couldn't all come to the same place, but they're scattered all over the country. You'd go to here, to…
Did you know a New Orleans gospel singer, Bessie Griffin? Bessie Griffin? Yeah, I knew. Is she still living?

Yeah, she's in California, out in Los Angeles now. Oh, she's out in Los Angeles. Remember she came to Chicago, remember Mahalia brought her to Chicago, and remember when we had the convention there in Chicago, Mahalia called, there were four great black gospel singers, women. One was Willa May Ford Smith, one was Bessie Griffin, one was Janice Jones, Ernestine Washington out of New York, and Mahalia. They were the top five divas of gospel music in the early days, and she was one of those. She was one of those.
